meta.headline: An editing copilot that lives in the timeline

path.role: Turns hours of footage into a cut that a producer approves
path.software: Timeline editor: media bins, source and program monitors, timeline, inspector
path.copilot: A panel beside the timeline; its rough cut lands as a new sequence

meta.oneLine: An editing copilot that lives in a panel inside the editing app, beside the timeline. It reads the open sequence, the playhead and the selected clips, finds takes and builds selects, drafts a rough cut as a new sequence, and waits for the editor before anything changes their own sequence or goes out for review.

role.summary: An editor turns hours of footage into a cut that a producer or client approves. On a team, an assistant editor ingests and organises the media first; the editor builds the story from rough cut to fine cut; review notes come back pinned to timecodes; after picture lock, color and sound take over.

measuredOn.text: A first cut to the producer by the deadline
Review rounds before approval (vague notes add rounds)
Deliverables on spec and on time

people.name: Assistant editor
people.relation: ingests, syncs and organises the media into bins

people.name: Producer or director
people.relation: reviews each cut and leaves notes at timecodes; approves the cut

people.name: Colorist and sound mixer
people.relation: take the locked cut; everything they do depends on picture lock

primary.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
primary.why: Where the cut is made: media organised in a project panel, a clip previewed in a source monitor, the sequence built on the timeline and played back in a program monitor.

around.name: Frame.io
around.why: Review: the cut goes up for comment, and reviewers' comments come back into the timeline as markers at the matching timecode.

around.name: Shared storage and proxies
around.why: Footage is backed up and turned into lighter proxy files before editing starts.

around.name: AI editing workspaces, such as Kino.ai
around.why: A newer category: an editing product where people and AI agents work on the same footage. It shows editors already accept AI inside the edit.

pattern.name: Timeline editor
pattern.summary: Everything sits around one sequence and is anchored to time. Media bins hold the footage; a source monitor previews one clip so the editor can mark the moment they want; the timeline holds the sequence as clips on video and audio tracks; a program monitor plays the sequence wherever the playhead sits. An inspector shows the settings of whatever is selected.
pattern.object: The sequence: clips on tracks over time, with markers
pattern.selection: Clips on the timeline, an in-to-out range, or a clip in a bin
pattern.open: One sequence on the timeline, one clip in the source monitor, the playhead's frame in the program monitor

regions.name: Media bins
regions.holds: Imported footage, audio and graphics, in folders

regions.name: Source monitor
regions.holds: One clip, before it goes into the cut
regions.does: Scrub, mark in and out, pick the take

regions.name: Program monitor
regions.holds: The sequence, playing from the playhead
regions.does: Watch the cut, judge the pacing

regions.name: Timeline
regions.holds: Clips on video and audio tracks, with markers
regions.does: Arrange, trim, cut, add titles and transitions

regions.name: Inspector
regions.holds: Settings of the selected clip: effects, motion, audio level

regions.name: Copilot panel
regions.holds: A plugin panel: the ask, the proposals and the gates
regions.does: Ask, review a proposal, apply or keep it

jobs.when: footage lands for a new project
jobs.want: have every clip transcribed, logged and tagged, with the best takes pulled into a selects bin
jobs.so: start on the story instead of scrubbing hours of footage
jobs.pain: Logging is slow, and poor organisation causes problems that grow later

jobs.want: start from a stringout built from the script or the best interview answers
jobs.so: react to a cut instead of a blank timeline
jobs.pain: The first pass is mostly mechanical

jobs.want: turn each note into a marker and a proposed change at its timecode
jobs.so: work through a round without missing a note

jobs.when: a producer asks whether we have a shot of something
jobs.want: search the footage by what's said and shown

jobs.when: I hand off to color and sound
jobs.want: prepare, label and export the locked sequence to their spec
jobs.so: hand off without questions coming back
jobs.pain: Late picture changes force rework downstream

jobs.want: have captions, versions and deliverables prepared to spec
jobs.so: deliver without a night of exports

flows.name: Footage to an approved cut
flows.trigger: a shoot's footage arrives on a drive
flows.outcome: a cut the producer has approved

steps.what: Ingests the media, backs it up, makes proxies and syncs sound.
Logs each clip (names, notes, transcripts, tags) and sorts it into bins, then hands the project over.
Scrubs the takes and marks the best moments into a selects sequence.
Builds the assembly, then the rough cut for story, then the fine cut for pacing.
Watches the cut and leaves notes at timecodes.
Brings the notes in as markers and works through them.
Approves the cut, or sends another round.

flows.timeGoes: Logging and finding the takes, before any story exists, then the wait between review rounds. Vague notes add rounds. The times here are Assumed: ask two editors how long each step takes on a real project.

write.what: Picture lock: the approved sequence is locked and exported for color and sound
write.who: The editor locks and exports it once the producer approves

flows.name: Picture lock to delivery

steps.what: Declares picture lock: no more picture changes.
Prepares and labels the tracks and exports for color and sound.
Grade the picture and mix the sound against the locked cut.
Brings back the graded picture and the mix, then adds captions.
Exports the masters and each social version.

flows.timeGoes: Rework when the picture changes after lock, and exporting versions one at a time.

surface.text: The copilot is a panel inside the editing app, docked beside the timeline under the inspector, so it sees what the editor sees: the open sequence, the playhead and the selection. Its work lands where an editor already looks: takes in a selects bin, a rough cut as a new sequence that plays in the program monitor, and markers at the timecodes it's talking about. In Premiere Pro it's a UXP plugin panel. Adobe says React runs in UXP panels after a build step; CopilotKit there is untested until the spike in C1.
surface.notThis: A chat window floating over the edit that can't see the sequence, answers "try cutting at 01:12" in text, and leaves the editor to make every change by hand.

reads.text: The open sequence: clips, tracks, in and out points, markers
reads.detail: Read through the editing app's plugin API (UXP in Premiere Pro) and sent with useAgentContext: clip ids, names and times, never the media itself

reads.text: The playhead position and the selected clips or range
reads.detail: What "this" and "here" mean when the editor asks

reads.text: Bin contents with their transcripts and tags
reads.detail: From the logging step: the copilot searches words and tags, not video frames

reads.text: Review notes as markers, with timecode and author
Project rules: delivery specs, naming, caption style

does.name: findTakes
does.text: Searches transcripts and tags for moments that match a description, such as every take where she mentions the launch.

does.name: buildSelects
does.text: Puts the matches into a selects bin, with in and out points.

does.name: proposeRoughCut
does.text: Builds a rough cut from the selects as a new sequence, through the plugin API, never editing the editor's own sequence.

does.name: addMarker
does.text: Adds a marker at a timecode, with a note.

does.name: movePlayhead
does.text: Jumps the playhead and the program monitor to the moment it's talking about.

renders.name: showTakes
renders.text: Take cards in the panel: a frame strip, the transcript line and the duration, with Play and Add to selects.
renders.detail: Interactive cards: Play opens the take in the source monitor

renders.name: showCutSummary
renders.text: A card for the proposed cut: clip count, length, which script beats it covers, and what it left out.

renders.name: showNotesRound
renders.text: One card per review round: each note, its timecode, the proposed change and whether it's done.

waits.name: applyToSequence
waits.text: Moving clips from the rough cut into the editor's own sequence: the card lists what it adds, moves and removes, with Apply or Keep as proposal.

waits.name: removeMedia
waits.text: Deleting or replacing any clip or media the editor placed.

waits.name: sendForReview
waits.text: Uploading a cut for the producer or client to review.

waits.name: exportDeliverables
waits.text: Rendering and delivering masters and versions.

shared.text: The proposal: a rough-cut sequence and a selects bin that both the editor and the copilot change. The editor's trims always win; the copilot re-reads them and never restores its own in-point.
shared.detail: The editing app's project is the shared record: tools read and write it through the plugin API, and the panel sends what changed with useAgentContext (or AG-UI agent state via useAgent if your agent owns the edit)

shared.text: Markers: both add them, and both mark review notes as done.

learns.text: Takes the editor rejects or re-trims from the copilot's selects.
Notes producers repeat across projects (keep titles inside the safe area, no jump cuts in interviews), proposed as a house rule that a lead editor publishes.
learns.detail: CopilotKit Intelligence; a person publishes before the rule takes effect

checklist.what: Prove CopilotKit runs in a panel inside the editing app
checklist.why: Everything else on this list assumes it, and a one-day spike settles it.
checklist.how: Build the React panel with UXP's build step, wrap it in CopilotKitProvider pointing at your runtime URL, and register one frontend tool that calls the plugin API.
checklist.done: A UXP panel in Premiere Pro chats with your runtime, and one tool adds a marker to the open sequence.

checklist.what: Put the sequence, the playhead and the selection in context
checklist.why: "Tighten this" only works if the copilot knows what "this" is.
checklist.how: Read the sequence's clip list, the playhead time and the selection through the plugin API, and register each as its own context entry. Send ids and times, not media.
checklist.done: Asking "what's under the playhead?" names the clip without the editor describing it.

checklist.what: Make the footage searchable as text, then give the copilot a search tool
checklist.why: The copilot searches transcripts and tags, not pixels; logging is the slowest part of the day.
checklist.how: Transcribe and tag clips at ingest in your pipeline; a findTakes frontend tool searches them and a buildSelects tool fills a selects bin.
checklist.done: "Every take where she mentions the launch" returns timecoded takes from the bins.

checklist.what: Draw takes as cards the editor can play and keep
checklist.why: An editor judges a take by watching it, not by reading about it.
checklist.how: Register showTakes as an interactive component: Play opens the take in the source monitor, Add puts it in selects.
checklist.done: Clicking Play on a take card cues it in the source monitor.

checklist.what: Propose the cut as a new sequence, never in the editor's own
checklist.why: The editor's sequence is the record; the copilot works beside it until someone says yes.
checklist.how: A proposeRoughCut tool builds a new sequence from the selects through the plugin API. Handlers read live state when they run.
checklist.done: The rough cut plays in the program monitor and the editor's own sequence is unchanged.

checklist.what: Gate every change to the real sequence
checklist.why: One wrong apply can wreck a day's cut; the editor decides.
checklist.how: applyToSequence as a human-in-the-loop card listing what it adds, moves and removes, with Apply or Keep as proposal.
checklist.done: Keep as proposal changes nothing; Apply changes exactly what the card listed.

checklist.what: Let the copilot hear the editor's trims
checklist.why: Shared work means the copilot reacts to the editor's changes and never undoes them.
checklist.how: When the editor trims a clip in the rough cut, post a short message and start a run; queue it while the agent is busy.
checklist.done: Re-trimming a clip in the rough cut makes the copilot acknowledge it and never restore its own in-point.

checklist.what: Turn a review round into a checklist of changes
checklist.why: Vague notes add rounds; a list with timecodes and status ends them.
checklist.how: Import notes as markers; the copilot proposes a change per note with addMarker and shows the round as a card.
checklist.done: Each imported note has a marker, a proposed change and a status, and the card shows what's left.

checklist.why: What leaves the edit suite reaches a producer or a client.
checklist.how: sendForReview and exportDeliverables as human-in-the-loop cards naming the version and the recipients.
checklist.done: Nothing is uploaded or exported without a click that names the version and who receives it.

checklist.what: Record rejected takes and repeated notes
checklist.why: The house style lives in producers' heads until it's written down.
checklist.how: Store each rejection and note with who and when; propose a house rule from repeats; a lead editor publishes it.
checklist.done: A note that comes back on three projects shows up as a proposed house rule a person can publish.

checklist.what: Watch the context and the tool calls in the web inspector while you build
checklist.why: When "tighten this" goes wrong, you need to see what the agent was told the selection was and which tool it picked.
checklist.how: Leave enableInspector on CopilotKitProvider in development: it shows the agent, the AG-UI events, the registered frontend tools and the shared context for each run.
checklist.done: During a run, the inspector shows the sequence, playhead and selection entries and each findTakes call.

who: An editor who cuts interviews or branded content every week
An assistant editor who ingests and logs footage
A producer who reviews cuts and leaves notes
ask: On a typical shoot day, how long do logging and finding the takes really take?
Would a copilot panel docked beside the timeline work for you, or would you rather call it from a command bar?
Would you let a copilot put clips on a ghost track? What would you need to see before you apply it?
How do review notes reach you today, and which are hardest to act on?
Which changes must never happen without your click: deleting media, replacing clips, exporting?
